questions.title: Bounded Max Finder
questions.description:
Bounded type parameters let a generic method compare values without knowing their exact type. A stock room reports the largest of its counts using a generic method declared as public static <T extends Comparable<T>> T maxOf(T[] arr) that loops with compareTo. Do not use Math.max anywhere.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are integers.

Output Format:
Print 'Max: v' where v is the largest value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; each value is between -1000000 and 1000000

questions.title: Count Matching Values
questions.description:
A survey tool counts how many readings satisfy a rule chosen at runtime. Write a generic method declared as public static <T> int countMatching(T[] arr, Predicate<T> pred) and call it with a lambda that tests whether a value is strictly greater than a threshold. Do not use streams.

Input Format:
One line: n, threshold, then n integers.

Output Format:
Print 'Count: c' where c is how many values are strictly greater than threshold.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; -1000000 <= values and threshold <= 1000000

questions.title: BiFunction Operation Chooser
questions.description:
A geometry panel lets users pick an operation by name and applies it to two operands. Store the named operations in a map as BiFunction<Double, Double, Double> lambdas (add, sub, mul) and dispatch with map.get instead of a switch statement.

Input Format:
One line: an operation (add, sub or mul) followed by two decimals.

Output Format:
Print the result with exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
-10000 <= operands <= 10000; op is add, sub or mul

questions.title: Generic Stack Simulator
questions.description:
Long before java.util.Stack, developers wrote their own. Build a generic Stack<T> class backed by a list with push, pop and peek methods (pop or peek on an empty stack returns null, and main then prints Empty), then replay the input operations.

Input Format:
The first token is n. Each of the next n operations is push x, pop or peek.

Output Format:
For each pop or peek print the resulting value, or Empty when the stack has no items.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; pushed values between -1000000 and 1000000; operations are push, pop or peek
questions.sampleinput1: 6 push 5 push 8 pop peek push 2 pop
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000; -1000000 <= pushed value <= 1000000; ops in {push, pop, peek}

questions.title: Supplier Shape Factory
questions.description:
A shape toolkit computes measurements lazily through factories. Define a generic method declared as public static <T> T produce(Supplier<T> factory) and build the chosen shape's formula as a Supplier<Double> lambda, then invoke it through produce. Use if-else selection, not a switch statement.

Input Format:
One line: a shape (circle, square or cube) and a decimal size (radius for circle, side for square and cube).

Output Format:
Print 'Label: v' with v to 2 decimals, where Label is 'Circle area' (pi*r*r), 'Square area' (s*s) or 'Cube volume' (s*s*s).

Constraints:
0 < size <= 1000

questions.title: Generic Array Reverser
questions.description:
A word game flips the order of tokens in place. Write a generic method declared as public static <T> void reverse(T[] arr) that swaps elements from both ends moving inward with a while loop, apply it to the input words, and print them space-separated on one line. Do not use Collections.reverse.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are words.

Output Format:
Print the words in reversed order, single-space separated, on one line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; words are single tokens of 1 to 15 characters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100; words are single tokens of 1-15 characters

questions.title: Mini Data Pipeline
questions.description:
A data tool chains three stages over an array of numbers: map each value with a Function lambda, filter the mapped values with a Predicate lambda, and fold the survivors with a custom functional interface BinOp { int combine(int a, int b); }. All three stages are chosen from the input, and no streams are used anywhere.

Input Format:
One line: n, then n integers, then mapOp (double, square or none), filterOp (even, positive or all) and reduceOp (sum, max or min).

Output Format:
Print 'Result: v' where v is the fold of the mapped values that pass the filter (fold starts from the first passing value). If nothing passes the filter print 'Result: empty'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; -1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100; -1000 <= value <= 1000; mapOp in {double, square, none}; filterOp in {even, positive, all}; reduceOp in {sum, max, min}

questions.title: Priority Shipping Queue
questions.description:
A shipping dock sorts parcels by weight using a priority queue. Define a small generic Parcel<T> class (T is the parcel id type, stored with an int weight and getId/getWeight accessors), build a Comparator<Parcel<String>> from the input ordering mode as a lambda (asc: lightest first, desc: heaviest first, ties broken by id in ascending alphabetical order), enqueue all parcels, then dequeue and print them in priority order. Do not use Collections.reverseOrder.

Input Format:
One line: mode (asc or desc), n, then n pairs of parcel id and integer weight.

Output Format:
Print each dequeued parcel as 'id weight' on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000; ids are unique tokens of 1 to 10 characters; 0 <= weight <= 10000
questions.inputconstrains: mode in {asc, desc}; 1 <= n <= 1000; ids unique 1-10 chars; 0 <= weight <= 10000

questions.title: Event Bus Dispatch
questions.description:
A smart home hub lets users register handlers for event names and later fires events through them. Build a Map<String, Consumer<String>> of handlers: upper prints 'UPPER: s' with the message capitalized, reverse prints 'REVERSE: s' with the message reversed using a manual loop (no StringBuilder.reverse), and echo prints 'ECHO: s'. Fire each event by dispatching through map.get, not a switch statement.

Input Format:
The first token is n, followed by n pairs of handler name and type (upper, reverse or echo). Then m, followed by m pairs of event name and message token.

Output Format:
For each fired event print the handler's output line, or 'No handler for name' when no handler is registered.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 20; names are 1 to 10 characters; messages are single tokens of 1 to 30 characters
questions.sampleinput1: 3 alert upper log reverse debug echo 3 alert fire log abcdef debug hello
questions.sampleoutput1:
UPPER: FIRE
REVERSE: fedcba
ECHO: hello
questions.sampleinput2: 1 beep echo 2 beep hi beep yo
questions.input1: 2 a upper b reverse 3 a cat b dog c bird
questions.output1:
UPPER: CAT
REVERSE: god
No handler for c
questions.input3: 2 x upper y echo 2 y hi x planet
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n, m <= 20; names 1-10 chars; handler types in {upper, reverse, echo}; messages 1-30 chars

questions.title: Serializer Registry
questions.description:
A reporting service serializes numbers differently depending on each field's type. Register each field tag with a Function<Integer, String> lambda in a map (plain: 'v=x', hex: '0x' followed by lowercase hex digits, binary: unsigned binary digits), then answer queries by dispatching through map.get without any instanceof checks.

Input Format:
The first token is n, followed by n pairs of tag and kind (plain, hex or binary). Then m, followed by m pairs of tag and integer value.

Output Format:
For each query print the serialized value, or 'Unknown type' when the tag is not registered.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10; 1 <= m <= 20; 0 <= value <= 1000000; tags are 1 to 10 characters
questions.sampleinput1: 3 score plain addr hex flags binary 3 score 42 addr 255 flags 10
questions.input1: 2 a hex b plain 3 a 16 b 0 c 9
questions.input3: 3 p plain h hex b binary 3 h 0 p 5 b 2
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 10; 1 <= m <= 20; kinds in {plain, hex, binary}; 0 <= value <= 1000000
